gaps.sentence: We'll be fine ___ the forecast is wrong.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless the forecast is wrong' = if it is not wrong.

gaps.sentence: If this medicine ___ relief within an hour, call me back.
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: does not bring.

gaps.sentence: As long as the budget ___, we can hire two more staff.
gaps.hint: as long as plus a passive condition
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' takes the present simple, here in the passive: is approved.

gaps.sentence: Had I realized the danger, I ___ the trip.
gaps.explanation: 'Had I realized …' = 'If I had realized …' + would have cancelled.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ late again, the manager will have to speak to you.
gaps.hint: a warning about a real future
gaps.explanation: A real warning about the future keeps the if-clause in the present simple: are.

gaps.sentence: You will not pass the course unless you ___ all the assignments.
gaps.hint: unless means if not, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces a negative condition and takes the present simple: complete.

gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: I will be surprised if he ___ on time for once.
gaps.explanation: The if-clause of a real future condition takes the present simple: arrives.
